literal: Shao also associated with Ang and his son Zhang in friendship. He once said to Zih Zhang, "I take you as the old clam that bore the pearl—do you wish the assembly all to bow to Ji Ke?
idiomatic: Xing Shao also befriended Lu Ang and his son Zhang. Once he said to Zhang, "I call you the old clam that bore the pearl—do you want everyone to bow to Ji Ke?

literal: " Thereupon his reputation rose daily; the refined scholar-gentry especially praised and upheld him.
idiomatic: " From this his reputation rose day by day; cultivated officials especially praised him.

literal: He began his career as Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; he served as secretary to Gao Cheng, Grand General; Secretariat Gentleman; concurrently Secretariat Vice Director; and in his regular post concurrently Crown Prince Preceptor.
idiomatic: He began as outer attendant of the scattered cavalry, then served as secretary to Grand General Gao Cheng, as secretariat gentleman and concurrent secretariat vice director, and in that post also as crown prince preceptor.

literal: From the time Liang and Wei made peace, each year brought mutual embassies; Ang each time held a concurrent post for banquet reception.
idiomatic: Once Liang and Wei were at peace, embassies were exchanged every year; Ang repeatedly held concurrent posts to host the banquets.

literal: At imperial banquets when composing verse, Ang always finished first; though his work was not fully polished, he was admired for quickness.
idiomatic: At imperial feasts when poems were set, Ang always finished first; though not always masterly, he was praised for his speed.

literal: He was appointed Secretariat Vice Director and edited the national history.
idiomatic: He was made secretariat vice director and edited the national history.

literal: On his father's death he left office; in mourning he fulfilled every rite, his grief wasting him to skin and bone.
idiomatic: He left office for his father's mourning and observed every rite until grief had wasted him to skin and bone.

literal: An edict recalled him to his former post.
idiomatic: An edict recalled him to his former post.

literal: When Gao Cheng held Ye, he prized Ang's utmost conduct and came in person to his gate to console and encourage him.
idiomatic: While Gao Cheng was stationed at Ye he admired Ang's conduct, came to his door in person, and comforted him.

literal: Ang's mother was the Wei Princess of Shangyong, first enfeoffed as Princess of Lantian—a woman of high principle and very strong resolve.
idiomatic: Ang's mother was the Wei princess of Shangyong, first enfeoffed as princess of Lantian—a woman of high principle and strong moral resolve.

literal: Ang had six brothers, all born of the mistress.
idiomatic: Ang and six brothers were all children of the same mother.

literal: Thus Xing Shao often told people, "Lantian breeds jade—indeed it is no empty saying.
idiomatic: Xing Shao often said, "Lantian breeds jade—the saying is no empty boast.

literal: " The mistress instructed her sons; all received righteous training. Though their crushing grief sprang from inborn nature, in action they still followed ritual measure—also their mother's instruction.
idiomatic: " Their mother trained them in the right way; though their overwhelming grief came from nature, they still acted by ritual—her teaching as well.

literal: Ang and his brothers together led huts by the tomb, carried earth to form the mound; the court deeply admired this, issued an edict of praise, and renamed their lane Xiaozhong Lane.
idiomatic: Ang and his brothers built mourning huts beside the tomb and heaped the grave with their own hands; the court admired them deeply, issued a commendation, and renamed their lane Xiaozhong, "Filial End."

literal: When mourning ended he was due to inherit, but he could not bear to succeed to the marquisate.
idiomatic: When mourning ended he was to inherit the title, but he could not bring himself to take the marquisate.

literal: At the start of Tianbao, the Prince of Changshan recommended Ang's talent and capacity; Gao Yang personally appointed him Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate Attendant, then promoted him to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: Early in Tianbao the prince of Changshan recommended Ang's ability; Gao Yang personally appointed him supervising secretary of the yellow gate attendant, then made him director of the ministry of personnel.

literal: Prince of Shangluo Sizong was magistrate of Qingdu; he summoned Ang as director of the district selection office and granted him the salary of Beiqiu county.
idiomatic: When Prince of Shangluo Sizong was magistrate of Qingdu he appointed Ang head of the local selection office with the salary of Beiqiu county.

literal: On his mother's death he mourned with such grief and wasting that he nearly could not survive the mourning; he fell critically ill, collapsed in a stupor, and lay on his pillow.
idiomatic: At his mother's death he grieved until he was near broken by mourning; he grew critically ill, collapsed in a stupor, and could not rise from his pillow.

literal: He also contracted a wind ailment.
idiomatic: He also contracted a wind disorder.

literal: His fifth younger brother Tuan, facing illness at life's end, told his brothers, "Our eldest brother's wasting illness is like this, and his nature is deeply loving. On the day of Tuan's death you must not let the eldest brother know; sounds of weeping must not be heard reaching through, lest it stir his grief.
idiomatic: His fifth brother Tuan, on his deathbed, told the others, "The eldest brother is this ill and tender-hearted. On the day I die you must not let him know; no weeping must reach him, or it will break his heart.

literal: " The family only told him when the funeral procession set out.
idiomatic: " The family told him only when the funeral cortege departed.

literal: Ang heard and grieved; one great sob and he died—forty-eight years old.
idiomatic: When Ang heard, he grieved; one great sob and he was gone, at forty-eight.

literal: Ang in court was earnest, cautious, and tight-lipped; he spoke no man's faults and boasted no merit of his own. His discourse was clear and far-reaching; he had discernment in human relations. Court and countryside deeply mourned him.
idiomatic: In office Ang was earnest and discreet; he spoke ill of no one and boasted of nothing. His speech was clear and measured, and he judged men well. Court and country mourned him deeply.

literal: He was posthumously made General of the Guards and inspector of Qing province; his posthumous title was Wen.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made general of the guards and inspector of Qing province, with the posthumous name Wen.

literal: His collected writings in fourteen scrolls circulated in the world.
idiomatic: His writings in fourteen scrolls circulated widely.

literal: Many of the Qi suburban-temple songs were composed by Ang.
idiomatic: Many of the Qi suburban-temple hymns were Ang's work.

literal: His son Yi succeeded and inherited the marquisate of Shiping.
idiomatic: His son Yi succeeded to the marquisate of Shiping.

literal: Wang Songnian was known from youth.
idiomatic: Wang Songnian was known from his youth.

literal: When Gao Cheng took Bingzhou he summoned him as secretary; he rose through posts to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and served as deputy to Li Wei on an embassy to Liang.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng took Bingzhou he made Songnian his secretary; he rose to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and went to Liang as deputy to Li Wei.

literal: On his return he held successive posts as director in the ministry.
idiomatic: After his return he served in successive director posts in the ministry.

literal: When Wei Shou finished compiling the Book of Wei, Songnian spoke slanderously of it; Gao Yang was angry, had him detained, and also had him beaten with the staff.
idiomatic: When Wei Shou completed the Book of Wei, Songnian spoke against it; Gao Yang was furious, had him imprisoned, and had him beaten.

literal: After more than a year he was released, appointed magistrate of Linzhang, then promoted to aide, chief administrator, and grand selection officer of his province.
idiomatic: After more than a year he was freed, made magistrate of Linzhang, then promoted to aide, chief administrator, and provincial grand selection officer.

literal: Gao Yan promoted him to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate Attendant.
idiomatic: Gao Yan promoted him to supervising secretary of the yellow gate attendant.

literal: Whenever the emperor granted him a seat and discussed state affairs with him, he was well pleased with him.
idiomatic: Whenever the emperor gave him a seat and discussed affairs, he favored him greatly.

literal: When Gao Yan died, Songnian galloped by post relay to Ye to proclaim the testament; as he spoke, tears streamed down, yet from the start of the proclamation to its end his bearing did not change and his words kept their rhythm.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan died, Songnian raced by post to Ye to proclaim the deathbed edict; he wept as he spoke, yet from beginning to end his composure did not alter and his delivery stayed measured.

literal: When the proclamation ended he wailed and threw himself to the ground; the hundred officials were all deeply moved.
idiomatic: When the reading ended he collapsed wailing; every official was moved.

literal: He returned to Jinyang, concurrently Palace Attendant, and escorted the coffin back to Ye.
idiomatic: He returned to Jinyang as concurrent palace attendant and escorted the coffin to Ye.

literal: The old ministers restrained their bearing; none dared show full grief—only Songnian wept with streaming tears, and the courtiers were all afraid.
idiomatic: Former ministers held themselves in check and none dared mourn openly; only Songnian wept freely, and courtiers were uneasy.

literal: Though Gao Zhan resented Songnian's deep attachment to the old reign, he also held him in high esteem.
idiomatic: Though Gao Zhan resented Songnian's loyalty to the late emperor, he still respected him.

literal: In his regular post he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, granted the salary of Gaoyi county, and took part in compiling laws and statutes; major affairs before and after were largely entrusted to him.
idiomatic: He was additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry with the salary of Gaoyi county, helped compile laws and statutes, and was entrusted with one major affair after another.

literal: He concurrently served as Imperial Censor.
idiomatic: He also served as imperial censor.

literal: Setting out from Jinyang for Ye, he fell ill on the road and died.
idiomatic: Leaving Jinyang for Ye, he fell ill on the road and died.

literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Personnel and inspector of Bing province; his posthumous title was Ping.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of personnel and inspector of Bing province, with the posthumous name Ping.

literal: The third son Shao was the most renowned.
idiomatic: The third son, Xing Shao, was the most famous.

literal: Liu Yi, style Yanying, was a man of Pengcheng.
idiomatic: Liu Yi, style Yanying, was from Pengcheng.

literal: His father Shiming had been Wei inspector of Yan province.
idiomatic: His father Shiming had been Wei inspector of Yan province.

literal: Yi's nature was broad and generous; he had weight and dignity; his bearing was admirable. Though intimate friends kept close company day and night, none failed to treat him with respect.
idiomatic: Yi was magnanimous and dignified, with a bearing men admired; even close friends who spent every day with him treated him with respect.

literal: He loved learning and was skilled in the Three Rites; rites of fortune and calamity especially held his attention.
idiomatic: He loved learning and excelled in the Three Rites, especially the ceremonies of fortune and mourning.

literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei he doffed his headcloth and became Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: In the Wei Xiaochang era he entered the academy as erudite.

literal: He rose through posts to inspector of Sui province; the frontier people submitted to his prestige and trust, and the borderlands knew great peace.
idiomatic: He rose to inspector of Sui province; frontier people trusted his authority and the border was at peace.

literal: When Gao Cheng held the regency he sent a letter of commendation, saying, "With your family's generations of loyal purity and successive generations in caps and coronets, worthy younger brothers and worthy sons all serve with me—hearts entrusted to one another, still as before.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng was regent he sent a letter of praise, saying, "Your house has been loyal for generations and worn court rank for ages; worthy brothers and sons serve at my side, and the trust between us is unchanged.

literal: You should exert your mind and strength to answer what is entrusted—do not worry that wealth and rank will not come.
idiomatic: Exert yourself to fulfill what I entrust to you; do not doubt that honor and wealth will follow.

literal: " When his term ended he went straight home to nurse his father's illness and never entered court.
idiomatic: " When his term ended he went home to tend his father's illness and never returned to court.

literal: On his father's death he was prostrate for years and could not rise without a staff.
idiomatic: After his father's death he lay prostrate for years and could not rise without a staff.

literal: Gao Cheng summoned him, but Yi pleaded illness and would not go.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng summoned him, but Yi pleaded illness and refused to come.

literal: Five sons—Xuan, Qi, Pu, Yuan, and Zan—all had resolve and principle and were praised by the age.
idiomatic: Five sons—Xuan, Qi, Pu, Yuan, and Zan—all had moral resolve and were praised in their time.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
